findings.reason: the section's own premise (it "runs after §8 merges") contradicts its `implementable` status; the author must either declare the facility-mint §8/§7 dependency in the meta and re-status §3, or name the resolved root/file by the mechanism that exists today, so the node does not start against owners that are absent.
findings.text: §3 states the root "comes from `imas_alambic/settings.py` `resolve_settings`" and the file name "from `pulse_writer.pulse_path`", presented as owners it reuses; opening the tree shows neither exists — there is no `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/settings.py`, `resolve_settings` and `IMAS_ALAMBIC_IDS_ROOT` appear nowhere in the repo, and `pulse_writer.py` defines no `pulse_path` (its leaf names are `write_pulse`/`IDS_NAMES`). Both are introduced by `jt60sa-facility-mint` §8 (`docs/plans/jt60sa-facility-mint.html:199-201`), which itself "waits for §7's rename to merge". §3 is nonetheless marked `data-status="implementable"` (plan.html:83) and this plan's `plan-section-depends-on` meta names only `imas-ink:ids-signal-traces#s1` (plan.html:23) — the §8 and §7 dependency is undeclared. So either §3 is not implementable as scoped, or §3 will re-implement the path resolution it claims to reuse.

findings.reason: the plan should name the one owner the reader lives on (extend `pulse_writer` to a read counterpart of `pulse_path`, or state that the two scripts' readers are deliberately distinct), so §3's restructure of one copy does not silently leave a divergent second one.
findings.text: `_read_pulse_ids(pulse_dir, ids_name)` opens `pulse_dir/{ids_name}.nc` through `imas.DBEntry`; the same mechanism is a second, independent copy at `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:45` `_read_ids(store_path, ids_name, dd_version)`. §3 reworks the signals copy (migrating it onto `pulse_path`) but the plan never names a single owner for "open one IDS from a per-IDS netCDF file", so the geometry copy stays behind and the two drift. Census of this defect type in the same pass: `scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py:37` (`_read_pulse_ids`) and `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:45` (`_read_ids`); the nearest owner that could be extended is `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/pulse_writer.py`, which owns the pulse layout but exposes only the write side (`write_pulse`).

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3 hides the whole open → `extract_signal_traces` → `time_trace_figure_mpl` → `render_to_bytes` chain behind one pulse-taking function returning the pulse's figure, an interface smaller than what it hides; the per-pulse output name is the only value it leaves to the caller. No spread of shallow wrappers is proposed.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 restructures the pulse-IDS reader in `scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py` without reconciling the second copy of the same "open one IDS from a `<ids>.nc` file via `imas.DBEntry`" mechanism already in the sibling figure script.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds no public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family (the new function is script-private), and it names what it retires: the module constants `SHOT`/`FIGURE`/`PULSE_DIR` (`scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py:32-34`) and the `JT60SA_ROOT` read for the pulse.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 names `imas_alambic/settings.py resolve_settings` and `pulse_writer.pulse_path` as the owners it reuses, but neither exists at HEAD; they are added by the unmerged `jt60sa-facility-mint` §8, which this plan's `plan-section-depends-on` meta does not declare.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the function's only added behaviour over imas-ink is the pulse-path open step, which imas-ink cannot own (it is ambix's placement concern); the plan extends the existing `_read_pulse_ids` site and calls `pulse_path` rather than forking a parallel reader, and it retires the E101154-fixed constants rather than layering over them.
